title: Geometrical Origin of Quantum Mechanics: The Inverted Cone and Formation of Fundamental Particles
content: We present a continuation of our cosmological model for the early universe. The model proposes that fundamental particles originate as spiraling threads of a hypothetical primordial s-particle distributed along the surface of a right-angled inverted cone in spacetime. We develop a formalism that directly maps particle rest masses to curvature trajectories on the conical surface. High curvature at the apex corresponds to massive dark matter, while lighter neutrinos occupy the outer rim, with remaining particles distributed between these positions according to the mass hierarchy of particle physics. Crucially, the model reveals that particle action is invariant along the entire conical path and quantized to exactly Planck’s constant h. This implies the particle’s physical loop circumference is identical to its quantum de Broglie wavelength. Mapping fermions (quarks and leptons) to the cone yields an angular momentum of ℏ/2. The requirement that particles maintain constant action while traversing varying curvature profiles along the inverted cone demonstrates that quantum mechanics is not merely a set of abstract rules, but rather emerges from a geometric perspective.
